summary.text: Diamond is a mineral made of carbon whose atoms are locked into a crystal pattern called diamond cubic.
Each carbon atom is bonded to four neighbours in rigid tetrahedra, packing more atoms into a given volume than any known substance and making diamond the hardest material.
Most natural diamonds formed 150 to 250 kilometres down in the mantle and were later carried to the surface by volcanic eruptions.

facts.label: Typical age
facts.value: Mostly between 1 and 3.5 billion years old

facts.label: Proof it is carbon
facts.value: Lavoisier burned one in 1772, producing only carbon dioxide

items.prompt: Diamond and graphite are both pure carbon. Why is graphite soft enough to use in pencils while diamond is the hardest material?

options.label: Graphite contains impurities that weaken it
Graphite's atom layers are weakly held and slide apart
Graphite's bonds between neighbouring atoms are weaker
Graphite forms at much lower temperatures

items.explain: Within a graphite layer the bonds are actually stronger than diamond's, but the layers are only weakly bonded to each other, so they slip past one another.

items.prompt: At ordinary room temperature and pressure, graphite is carbon's stable form. What happens to a diamond ring left in a drawer?

options.label: It slowly dissolves in the air's moisture
It turns to graphite within a few decades
It gradually becomes harder over the years
Its change to graphite is far too slow to notice

items.explain: Diamond is metastable: an energy barrier keeps its atoms in place, so conversion to graphite takes millions to billions of years.

items.prompt: Someone sets a diamond in pure oxygen and focuses sunlight on it with a lens. What is left after it burns?

options.label: Only carbon dioxide gas
A small lump of graphite
Glassy ash of silicon
Water vapour and smoke

items.explain: Lavoisier did exactly this in 1772; the only product was carbon dioxide, showing diamond is made of carbon.

items.prompt: A jeweller has a blue diamond. What most likely gives it its colour?

options.label: A thin coating of copper on its surface
Tiny traces of boron among its carbon atoms
Large amounts of iron mixed into the crystal
Light reflecting off water trapped inside

items.explain: About one impurity atom per million is enough; boron turns a diamond blue and nitrogen turns it yellow.

items.prompt: Diamonds formed deep in the mantle, far below where anyone can dig. How did they reach places where people mine them?

options.label: Rivers eroded the mantle and washed them upward
Meteorite impacts threw them up from below
Volcanic eruptions carried them to the surface
They slowly floated up because they are light

items.explain: Hundreds to tens of millions of years ago, eruptions brought them up and left them in rocks called kimberlites and lamproites.

items.prompt: A lab needs a material to spread heat away from a hot electronic part as fast as possible. Why might it pick diamond?

options.label: It conducts electricity better than metals
It melts away and absorbs the heat
It reflects heat back toward its source
It conducts heat better than any other natural material

items.explain: Diamond has the highest thermal conductivity of any natural material, while being a poor conductor of electricity.
